# S258 — Spec check row: ork picks it by a setting, offers the fix when it is missing, and keeps it out of the lineups

*Proposed.* A project names the matrix rows its spec check runs on with a project setting. Every row so named, and the row the u11 rule names, stays out of the reviewer and gate chains. When a project has neither, the spec check fails with an owner-facing error (not `internal:`) that gives the exact command to fix it. How the setting looks is open (Q1); the spec below is written for the recommended answer.

**Findings:** 2026-11-03: (1) A wave launch on the slicer project failed with 'internal: the matrix has no Spec check row: add a rule that names it as Spec check row (rNN)'. The matrix had no such rule; the owner had me add r18 and rule u10 there. The adjudicate, daystar, pitfight and squalify matrices have none either (read from their relay-roles files; use 'slicer relay-roles show --root' to confirm). The message is prefixed 'internal:' although the owner can fix it, and the TUI offers no fix: it could show the exact add and rule-add commands, or a setup step in the S251 settings pane. (2) Ork finds the row only through a rule that matches Spec check row (rNN) (internal/slicercli/write.go:254), and skips only that row, the UI pass row and unknown agents when it builds the reviewer and gate chains (internal/daemon/runs.go:381-405). A second spec-check row on a vendor ork runs (for example a terra row, owner request 2026-11-03) would leak into the reviewer and gate chains and cannot be picked for the spec check. Needed: a way to choose among spec-check rows (a project setting or a note marker on the row), and every spec-check row skipped from the chains. The owner decides the marker. Related: S116, S167, S251. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-07** — Owner answer (2026-11-07): (1) with no spec_check_rows setting, every rule-named row is a spec-check fallback in rule order (SpecCheckRowIDs), not only the first. (2) The no_spec_check_row message and the guide warn that a row listed in spec_check_rows leaves every run's reviewer and gate chains. (3) The message is multi-line: the problem, then a fix line, then an or line, then the candidate rows, with real candidate ids in place of rNN.

## Why

Findings, 2026-11-03 (owner session): a wave launch on the slicer project failed with `internal: the matrix has no Spec check row: add a rule that names it as Spec check row (rNN)`. The slicer matrix had no such rule; the owner had r18 and a rule added there. The adjudicate, daystar, pitfight and squalify matrices had none either (per the findings; not re-read here). The owner can fix this, yet the text says `internal:`, and the TUI offers no fix. Related: S116, S167, S251.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-07 at a1114e2):

- ork finds the row only through a rule whose text matches `Spec check row (rNN)`, and takes the first match (`specCheckRow` and `SpecCheckRowID`, `internal/slicercli/write.go:254-266`).
- `specChain` (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:86-124`) returns a plain `errors.New` when no rule names a row (`:96`) and a plain `fmt.Errorf` when the row is not among the recommended reviewer rows (`:121`). `ipc.ErrorOf` turns a plain error into code `internal` (`internal/ipc/ipc.go:71`), and the TUI prints `CODE: message` (`internal/tui/model.go:1788`); the CLI prints the code too (`internal/cli/cli.go:212`). That is where `internal:` comes from.
- The run plan skips only the one row `SpecCheckRowID` returns, the UI pass row and rows with no adapter when it builds the reviewer and gate chains (`internal/daemon/runs.go:395`, `:420-422`). `roles.matrix` labels only that row (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:50`, `:83`).
- The ork matrix today (`slicer relay-roles show`, 2026-11-07): rule u11 names r16 (Claude sonnet high) as the Spec check row. r24 (Grok, latest, medium) is a reviewer row whose note says "Spec check row on Grok ... an alternative to r16", but no rule names it. So r24 is not skipped: it can enter the reviewer and gate chains, and it cannot be picked for the spec check. This is the leak the findings describe for a second spec-check row.
- The registry has no field for this (`internal/registry/registry.go:207-234`); project settings go through `projects.set` (`internal/daemon/wire.go:276`, `internal/daemon/handlers.go:538-604`) and `ork projects set` (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:273-288`).
- The design says the lineup row is the one the u11 rule names (`docs/design.md:861-863`).

Boundary: the matrix is slicer's; ork reads it through `slicer relay-roles show` and never edits it. Which row ork runs for its own spec check is ork's policy, so the setting is ork's registry (Q1).

Open question Q1 (open, 2026-11-07; owner to answer): how does a project name its spec check rows?
- (a) A registry setting naming one row: `spec_check_row: "r16"` (`ork projects set NAME --spec-check-row r16`).
- (b) A registry setting naming an ordered list: `spec_check_rows: ["r16", "r24"]` (`--spec-check-rows r16,r24`). The first row with an adapter runs; the next is its fallback; every listed row is kept out of the reviewer and gate chains.
- (c) A marker in the row's note in slicer's matrix (for example a note that starts `Spec check row`), with no ork setting.
Recommendation: (b). It covers r16 with r24 as its fallback, fixes the r24 leak with one setting, and keeps ork from parsing note prose. When the setting is unset, ork keeps today's rule (the u11 rule's row), so no project breaks.

Open question Q2 (open; owner to answer): the error code for "no spec check row". Options: (a) a new code `no_spec_check_row` (*proposed*); (b) the existing `bad_params`. Recommendation: (a): the TUI can match it and offer the fix; `bad_params` names a caller's mistake, which this is not.

- `TestSpecCheckRowIDsListsEveryNamedRow` (`internal/slicercli/rules_test.go`): two rules naming r16 and r24 give `["r16", "r24"]`; `SpecCheckRowID` still gives `r16`. Fails first: no `SpecCheckRowIDs`.
- `TestSpecChainUsesTheProjectSetting` (`internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go`): `spec_check_rows: ["r24", "r16"]` with a matrix whose rule names r16: the chain is r24's entry then r16's. Fails first: the chain is r16 only.
- `TestSpecChainFallsBackToTheRuleWhenUnset`: no setting: the u11 rule's row, as today (guard).
- `TestSpecChainWithoutARowIsAnOwnerError`: no setting and no rule: the error has code `no_spec_check_row`, not `internal`, and its message names `ork projects set NAME --spec-check-rows rNN` and the reviewer rows with an adapter. Fails first: code `internal`.
- `TestSpecChainRowNotRecommendedIsAnOwnerError`: the set row is not among the recommended reviewer rows: same code, the message names the row.
- `TestPlanKeepsEverySpecCheckRowOutOfEveryChain` (extend `TestPlanKeepsTheSpecCheckRowOutOfEveryChain`, `speccheck_test.go:366`): the setting names r24 and the rule names r16: neither appears in the reviewer or gate chain. Fails first: r24 is in the chains.
- `TestMatrixLabelsEverySpecCheckRow` (`internal/daemon`): `roles.matrix` gives `Spec check row, ...` for r16 and r24.
- `TestProjectsSetSpecCheckRows` (`internal/daemon` and `internal/cli`): set, read back, `[]` clears; `r1x` and `16` are `bad_params`.
- `TestRegistryKeepsSpecCheckRows` (`internal/registry`): round trip; an empty list is not written.

## Implement

1. Wait for Q1 and Q2. Then tests first; see each fail for the reason given.
2. Registry field and validator; `projects.set` and `ork projects set --spec-check-rows`.
3. `slicercli.SpecCheckRowIDs`.
4. One daemon helper, for example `specCheckRows(proj, rules) []string`: the setting when set, else `SpecCheckRowIDs(rules)`. `specChain` builds its chain from it, in order, from the recommended reviewer rows. The run plan and `roles.matrix` skip and label every id it returns plus every id the rules name.
5. The two `specChain` errors become `&ipc.Error{Code: "no_spec_check_row", Message: ...}`. The message says what is missing and gives the command: `ork projects set NAME --spec-check-rows rNN` (or adding a `Spec check row (rNN)` rule with `slicer relay-roles rule-add`), and lists the reviewer rows with an adapter.
6. Docs (mark the setting *proposed*) and the CHANGELOG entry last.
7. Do not edit any matrix, do not parse row notes, and do not touch `internal/tui` or `internal/engine`.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). Q1: option (b), an ordered list setting spec_check_rows (ork projects set NAME --spec-check-rows r16,r24). The first row with an adapter runs, the next is its fallback, and every listed row stays out of the reviewer and gate chains. When the setting is unset, ork keeps today's u11 rule. Q2: a new error code no_spec_check_row with an owner-facing message that gives the exact fix command.
